venues.name: Aman Venice
venues.note: Aman's Venetian house, a 16th-century Grand Canal palazzo with Tiepolo ceilings and just 24 rooms, private to the point of silence.

venues.name: Cipriani, A Belmond Hotel, Venice
venues.note: The first hotel Belmond ever owned, an island retreat with an Olympic saltwater pool and its own launch to St Mark's.

venues.name: The St. Regis Venice
venues.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near San Moisè)
venues.note: A run of restored palazzi on the Grand Canal, contemporary within, butler service and a waterfront terrace facing Santa Maria della Salute.

venues.name: Hotel Metropole
venues.note: A waterfront landmark packed with a collector's rooms of art and antiques, intensely, idiosyncratically Venetian.

venues.name: Nolinski Venezia, Evok Collection
venues.note: Paris meets Venice in the former stock-exchange building off the square, the city's most fashionable recent opening.

venues.name: Ca' Sagredo Hotel
venues.note: A 15th-century palazzo and national monument on the Grand Canal, hung with frescoes by Tiepolo and Longhi, a stay inside a museum.
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World

venues.name: Violino d'Oro
venues.area: San Marco (near San Moisè / Grand Canal)
venues.note: An intimate, beautifully-crafted boutique house on a small canal square, a short walk from Piazza San Marco.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Ca' di Dio
venues.area: Castello (Riva Ca' di Dio, near the Arsenale)
venues.note: A 13th-century pilgrims' hospice reimagined by Patricia Urquiola, two courtyards and a calm well away from the crowds.

venues.name: Londra Palace Venezia
venues.note: A lagoon-front palazzo where Tchaikovsky wrote his Fourth Symphony, 53 windows onto the water, freshly and elegantly redone.

venues.name: Hotel Bauer / Rosewood Venice
venues.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, Campo San Moisè)
venues.note: The historic Bauer on the Grand Canal, reborn under Rosewood, a landmark palazzo restoration steps from the square.

venues.name: The Venice Venice Hotel
venues.area: Cannaregio (Grand Canal, near Ca' d'Oro / Rialto)
venues.note: A 13th-century palazzo turned 'post-Venetian' design hotel on the Grand Canal, art, vintage and a canal-level lounge.

venues.name: Palazzo Venart Luxury Hotel
venues.area: Santa Croce (Grand Canal, near San Stae)
venues.note: A frescoed Grand Canal palazzo with a private garden, home to the city's most decorated kitchen.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Hotel Excelsior Venice Lido Resort
venues.note: A Moorish-fantasy beach palace on the Lido, the grand address of the Venice Film Festival, with a private stretch of Adriatic sand.

venues.name: JW Marriott Venice Resort & Spa
venues.note: A whole private lagoon island with a rooftop pool, olive groves and a spa, resort calm, ten minutes by launch from the square.

venues.name: Hotel Cipriani, Palazzo Vendramin & Palazzetto
venues.note: The Cipriani's private annexe of grand suites, with a butler and lagoon-facing salon looking straight at San Marco.
credentials: MICHELIN Three Keys (2025, as part of Belmond Hotel Cipriani)

venues.name: Baglioni Hotel Luna
venues.area: San Marco (near Piazza San Marco / St Mark's Basin)
venues.note: Reputedly the oldest hostelry in Venice, moments from the square, with a Tiepolo-school frescoed ballroom.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Hotel Danieli Excelsior wing / Hotel Monaco & Grand Canal
venues.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near San Marco Vallaresso)
venues.note: A Grand Canal house at the mouth of the basin, the Ridotto's old gaming rooms within, and a terrace on the water.

venues.name: Palazzina Grassi
venues.area: San Marco (Grand Canal, near Campo San Samuele)
venues.note: Philippe Starck's playful design palazzo on the Grand Canal, the city's most fashionable small hotel.

venues.name: Hotel Flora
venues.area: San Marco (near Calle Larga XXII Marzo)
venues.note: A family-run garden hideaway off the smart shopping street, a pocket of green calm in the middle of San Marco.

venues.name: NH Collection Venezia Palazzo Barocci
venues.note: A restored Gothic palazzo on the Grand Canal with canal-view rooms, grand address, gentler price.

venues.name: Hotel Ai Reali
venues.note: A quietly luxurious small hotel just off the Rialto, with a rare indoor pool and spa for Venice.
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World

venues.name: Splendid Venice, Starhotels Collezione
venues.note: A comfortable, characterful house in the heart of San Marco, with a roof terrace over the tiled skyline.

venues.name: Glam, Enrico Bartolini
venues.note: Enrico Bartolini's Venetian two-star, the city's most decorated kitchen, in a frescoed palazzo with a canal garden.

venues.name: Oro Restaurant
venues.note: Fine Italian cooking inside the Cipriani, the meal begins with a private launch across the water from San Marco.

venues.name: Quadri
venues.note: The Alajmo family's grand room on St Mark's Square itself, the only starred table with that view.

venues.name: Venissa
venues.note: Chiara Pavan and Francesco Brutto's 'environmental cuisine' in a walled medieval vineyard, the lagoon on a plate.

venues.name: Local
venues.note: Chef Salvatore Sodano's minimalist, open-kitchen room, one of the most exciting tables in Venice.

venues.name: Wistèria
venues.area: San Polo (Rio de la Frescada, near the Frari)
venues.note: Seasonal contemporary cooking under the wisteria on a quiet lateral canal, intimate and quietly assured.

venues.name: Il Ridotto
venues.area: Castello (near Campo SS. Filippo e Giacomo, off St Mark's)
venues.note: Just nine tables a short stroll from the Basilica, refined Venetian cooking on an intimate scale.

venues.name: Vini da Gigio
venues.note: A rustic family inn where you can see into the kitchen, proper Venetian fish and meat, and a serious cellar.

venues.name: Osteria Anice Stellato
venues.note: Imaginative Venetian cooking in the quiet north of Cannaregio, modern takes on regional classics.

venues.name: Al Covo
venues.note: A long-loved husband-and-wife room devoted to lagoon fish and unfussy, precise Venetian cooking.

venues.name: Ai Gondolieri
venues.note: A rare Venetian rarity, a meat-focused kitchen, in the museum quarter near the Guggenheim.

venues.name: Trattoria Alla Madonna
venues.note: A vast, buzzing Rialto institution since 1954, the classic Venetian fish trattoria, done at scale and done well.

venues.name: Antiche Carampane
venues.area: San Polo (Rio Terà de le Carampane)
venues.note: A hard-to-find, family-run fish osteria beloved by those in the know, no pizza, no menu turistico, no compromise.

venues.name: Estro Vino e Cucina
venues.note: A modern wine-bar-and-kitchen from two brothers, natural wines and sharp, contemporary Venetian small plates.

venues.name: Osteria alle Testiere
venues.note: Barely two dozen seats and an ever-changing chalkboard of the day's lagoon catch, a purist's fish room.

venues.name: CoVino
venues.note: A slow-food micro-restaurant with a short, daily-changing set menu and a thoughtful natural wine list.
credentials: Slow Food, recognised; MICHELIN Guide area listing

venues.name: Trattoria Al Gatto Nero
venues.note: Burano's most famous kitchen, the risotto de gò (goby-fish risotto) that draws chefs across the lagoon.

venues.name: Harry's Bar
venues.note: Cipriani's 1931 original, the birthplace of the Bellini and carpaccio, and a declared national landmark.
credentials: Declared a national landmark by Italy's Ministry of Culture (2001)

venues.name: Cip's Club
venues.note: The Cipriani's terrace trattoria on the water's edge, pasta and Bellinis with San Marco laid out across the basin.
credentials: Within Belmond Hotel Cipriani (MICHELIN Three Keys)

venues.name: Ristorante Riviera
venues.note: A refined room on the Zattere waterfront looking to the Giudecca canal, polished Venetian cooking at sunset.

venues.name: All'Arco
venues.note: The benchmark cicchetti counter by the Rialto market, a stand-up plate of the day's best, done impeccably.
credentials: Widely cited as Venice's finest bacaro; Slow Food / press-recognised

venues.name: Cantine del Vino già Schiavi (Al Bottegon)
venues.note: A cult wine bar and cicchetti counter by the gondola boatyard, inventive crostini and a wall of bottles.
credentials: Cited among Venice's great bacari; Slow Food / press-recognised

venues.name: St Mark's Basilica (Basilica di San Marco)
venues.note: Venice's golden cathedral, over 8,000 sq m of Byzantine mosaics glinting above the nave, the jewelled Pala d'Oro altarpiece and the four bronze horses. Book a timed skip-the-line slot and add the Loggia terrace for the horses and a view over the square; shoulders and knees must be covered, and a private guide keeps a multi-generational group moving past the crowds.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Doge's Palace (Palazzo Ducale)
venues.note: The pink-and-white Gothic seat of the Venetian Republic, vast council chambers hung with Tintoretto and Veronese, the golden Scala d'Oro staircase, then across the enclosed Bridge of Sighs to the old prisons. The Secret Itineraries tour (book ahead) takes you through the doge's private routes and Casanova's cell.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Piazza San Marco
venues.note: Napoleon's 'drawing room of Europe', the only true piazza in Venice, framed by the arcaded Procuratie and the basilica. Come at first light for the empty square to yourselves, or take coffee at Caffè Florian (since 1720) with the orchestra playing; the pigeon-fed grandchildren will remember it for life.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: St Mark's Campanile
venues.note: The 98.6m bell tower of the basilica, rebuilt after its 1902 collapse, with a lift straight to the top. The finest panorama in the city, the whole lagoon, the red rooftops and San Giorgio across the water; go near sunset and book the timed ticket to skip the queue.

venues.name: Torre dell'Orologio (St Mark's Clock Tower)
venues.note: The Renaissance astronomical clock tower of 1499 above the entrance to the Mercerie, showing moon phases and the zodiac, topped by the two bronze 'Moors' who strike the hour. Visit only by pre-booked guided tour, which climbs inside past the working mechanism to the terrace beside the bell.

venues.name: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute
venues.note: Longhena's great white baroque dome at the mouth of the Grand Canal, built in thanks for the end of the 1630 plague. Step inside the octagon for Titian's ceiling canvases and 'Pentecost'; it is a two-minute walk from the Punta della Dogana, so pair the two on one Dorsoduro morning.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Basilica dei Frari (Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari)
venues.note: The towering brick Franciscan church that holds Titian's radiant 'Assumption of the Virgin' over the high altar, and Titian's own tomb, and Canova's pyramid monument. Quiet, cool and profoundly moving; combine with the Scuola Grande di San Rocco a minute away.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: San Giorgio Maggiore
venues.note: Palladio's serene white Benedictine church on its own island facing the piazzetta, with two Tintorettos in the chancel. Take the lift up the campanile for the classic postcard view back across the water to San Marco, far shorter queues than St Mark's own tower.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Gallerie dell'Accademia
venues.note: The definitive collection of Venetian painting from the 14th to 18th centuries, Bellini, Giorgione, Carpaccio, Titian, Tintoretto, Veronese, and Leonardo's 'Vitruvian Man' (shown only occasionally). The anchor of the Dorsoduro 'Museum Mile'; a private guide makes two hours plenty for a family.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Peggy Guggenheim Collection
venues.note: Peggy Guggenheim's unfinished palazzo on the Grand Canal, packed with Picasso, Pollock, Ernst, Miró, Kandinsky and Calder, plus a sculpture garden by the water. Human-scaled and light-filled, the easiest modern-art hit in Venice, with a cafe terrace for a break.

venues.name: Ca' Rezzonico (Museum of 18th-Century Venice)
venues.note: A Longhena palazzo opening straight onto the Grand Canal, restored as a museum of Settecento Venice, Tiepolo ceilings, Longhi's scenes of daily life, Murano chandeliers and a reconstructed apothecary. Grand and uncrowded; the ballroom alone justifies the visit.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Punta della Dogana
venues.note: The triangular former customs house at the tip of Dorsoduro, converted by Tadao Ando into a raw, luminous space for the Pinault Collection's contemporary art, Hirst, Sherman and other living names. Book jointly with its sister venue Palazzo Grassi.

venues.name: Palazzo Grassi
venues.note: The grandest 18th-century palace on the Grand Canal, also remodelled by Tadao Ando, staging large single-artist and thematic shows from the Pinault Collection. A calm, monumental counterpoint to the old-master churches nearby.

venues.name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
venues.note: A confraternity hall entirely covered by more than 50 Tintoretto canvases, his life's masterwork, from the vast 'Crucifixion' to the ceiling cycle. Grab one of the mirrors provided so you can study the ceilings without craning; a minute from the Frari.

venues.name: Grand Canal by vaporetto Line 1
venues.note: The world's most beautiful high street, a slow ride the full length of the Grand Canal past a parade of Gothic and Renaissance palazzi, under the Rialto and Accademia bridges. Sit at the open stern of the Line 1 boat; or, discreetly, hire a private water taxi to run it at your own pace.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Gondola ride through the back canals
venues.note: The essential Venetian half-hour, glide off the Grand Canal into the silent narrow rii, under low bridges, past water-doors. Start away from the San Marco rank to avoid the jam; a private evening ride with your own boatman is the calm, romantic version for a couple or a family of four.

venues.name: Traghetto crossing of the Grand Canal
venues.note: The locals' shortcut, a two-euro, two-minute crossing of the Grand Canal standing up in a shared gondola, at points like Santa Sofia near the Rialto. The cheapest, most authentic gondola moment there is, and a small thrill for children learning to balance like a Venetian.

venues.name: Rialto Bridge (Ponte di Rialto)
venues.note: The oldest and grandest of the canal's four bridges, a single marble arch of 1591 lined with shops, framing the classic Grand Canal view of boats and palazzi. Cross at dawn for the empty stone; by day it is the busy hinge between San Marco and the market side.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Rialto Market (Mercato di Rialto)
venues.note: Venice's larder for a thousand years, the Erberia fruit-and-vegetable stalls and the arcaded Pescheria fish market, busiest and best before 9am (closed Sundays, fish also Mondays). A feast of colour for the eye even without buying; the surrounding lanes hide bacari for a cicchetti graze.

venues.name: T Fondaco dei Tedeschi rooftop terrace
venues.note: The rooftop of the restored German merchants' house, now a luxury store beside the Rialto, opens a free 360° terrace over the bend of the Grand Canal. Slots are timed and must be booked ahead online, do it, it is the best free view in Venice.

venues.name: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
venues.note: A hidden multi-arched spiral staircase (bovolo means 'snail shell') tucked in a courtyard near Campo Manin, climbing to a loggia with a rooftop view over the tiled sea of the city. A short, quiet, magical detour that most day-trippers never find.

venues.name: Libreria Acqua Alta
venues.note: The gloriously chaotic bookshop that stacks its stock in gondolas and bathtubs against the high water, with resident cats and a 'staircase' of old books out the back leading to a canal view. Photogenic and one-of-a-kind, children love the cats and the flooded absurdity of it.

venues.name: Jewish Ghetto (Ghetto Ebraico)
venues.note: The world's first ghetto, established in 1516, tall, crowded houses around a quiet campo, five historic synagogues and the Jewish Museum, with kosher bakeries and restaurants nearby. Take the museum's synagogue tour to understand a moving chapter of the city's history.

venues.name: Cannaregio sestiere and the Fondamenta della Misericordia
venues.note: The city's most lived-in quarter, long sunny canalside fondamente lined with bacari, washing strung overhead, real Venetians going about their day. Come for an early-evening cicchetti-and-ombra crawl where the locals eat, a world away from the San Marco crush.

venues.name: Madonna dell'Orto
venues.note: Tintoretto's parish church in quiet northern Cannaregio, holding several of his greatest canvases and his tomb. Serene, uncrowded and richly rewarding, the sort of place a private guide brings you to feel the real Venice between the headline sights.

venues.name: Ca' d'Oro (Galleria Giorgio Franchetti)
venues.note: The 'golden house', the most beautiful Gothic palace on the Grand Canal, now a gallery whose treasures include Mantegna's 'St Sebastian'. Step onto its canal-side loggia for a rare inside-a-palazzo view straight down the water.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Dorsoduro and the Zattere waterfront
venues.note: Venice's arty, student quarter, the buzzing Campo Santa Margherita by night, and the long, sunlit Zattere promenade along the Giudecca Canal with wide water views. A gelato on the Zattere at sunset is one of the city's simplest pleasures for all ages.

venues.name: Squero di San Trovaso
venues.note: One of the last working gondola boatyards, its Alpine-style wooden sheds set against a quiet canal in Dorsoduro. You watch the craftsmen from across the water as they build and repair the black boats by hand, a living workshop, best viewed from the Fondamenta opposite.

venues.name: Castello and the Via Garibaldi
venues.note: The broad, tree-lined Via Garibaldi in eastern Castello is where Venetians shop, gossip and eat, the least touristy stroll in the city, leading to the leafy public gardens. A genuine neighbourhood walk that grandparents and grandchildren can amble at their own pace.

venues.name: Scuola Dalmata di San Giorgio degli Schiavoni
venues.note: A tiny confraternity hall in Castello whose ground-floor room is wrapped in Vittore Carpaccio's jewel-like narrative cycle of St George and the dragon and St Jerome. One of the most intimate and perfect small treasures in all Venice.

venues.name: Chiesa di San Zaccaria
venues.note: Just behind the waterfront, this church holds Giovanni Bellini's luminous altarpiece 'San Zaccaria Altarpiece', and, for a small fee, a flooded crypt you can descend into among the old doges' tombs. An easy, atmospheric stop steps from San Marco.

venues.name: Teatro La Fenice
venues.note: 'The Phoenix', the opera house that has burned and risen more than once, restored in gilt and blue after the 1996 fire. Take the daytime audio-guided tour of the auditorium and royal box, or, better, book a night at the opera and dress for it.

venues.name: Riva degli Schiavoni promenade
venues.note: The grand waterfront esplanade sweeping east from the Doge's Palace, crossing pretty bridges past the great old hotels, with the lagoon and San Giorgio filling the view. The best evening passeggiata in the city, wide, open and unhurried.

venues.name: Bridge of Sighs (Ponte dei Sospiri) viewpoint
venues.note: The enclosed white baroque bridge of 1603 that carried prisoners from the Doge's Palace to the new prisons, the last glimpse of the lagoon they 'sighed' over. See it from the Ponte della Paglia on the waterfront; you cross it from inside on the palace tour.

venues.name: Murano, glass island
venues.note: The lagoon island where Venetian glass has been blown since 1291, watch a live furnace demonstration, tour the Museo del Vetro, and buy directly from the historic furnaces. Arrange a private furnace visit and shipping for a serious chandelier or sculpture; a short vaporetto or water-taxi hop from Fondamente Nove.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Burano, lace and painted houses
venues.note: The most photogenic island in the lagoon, a village of vividly painted fishermen's houses along little canals, and a centuries-old lace tradition shown in the Museo del Merletto. Lunch on lagoon fish here (veg-friendly risottos too), and let the family wander the rainbow lanes.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Torcello, the oldest island
venues.note: Where Venice began, a near-empty island of grass and reeds with the ancient Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta and its extraordinary Byzantine golden mosaics, plus the climbable campanile. Wonderfully peaceful; pair it with Burano next door, or lunch at the storied Locanda Cipriani.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: San Michele, the cemetery island
venues.note: The walled island cemetery between Venice and Murano, entered through Codussi's pure white Renaissance church, with cypress avenues and the graves of Stravinsky, Diaghilev and Ezra Pound. A quiet, contemplative half-hour on the way to Murano.

venues.name: The Lido di Venezia
venues.note: The long sandbar barrier island of beaches and Liberty-era villas, home each September to the Venice Film Festival and the belle-époque grand hotels. Cycle the seafront, take a cabana for a beach day with the children, or dine at the historic Excelsior, a complete change of pace from the stone city.

venues.name: Venice Biennale (in season)
venues.note: The world's most important art (and, alternate years, architecture) exhibition, spread across the leafy Giardini national pavilions and the vast brick halls of the Arsenale, roughly May to November. The 2026 art edition runs 9 May–22 November; a guided half-day makes the sprawling Arsenale manageable.

venues.name: The Arsenale
venues.note: The colossal medieval shipyard that built the Republic's fleet, walled, gated by monumental lions, and one of the great sights of industrial history. Much of it opens during the Biennale; the imposing land gate and the lion-guarded entrance repay a look any time.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Fondazione Querini Stampalia
venues.note: A patrician palazzo-museum near Santa Maria Formosa, famous for Carlo Scarpa's exquisite modernist ground floor and garden woven around the canal water. A refined, little-known stop for lovers of art and design, blissfully quiet.

venues.name: Basilica dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo (San Zanipolo)
venues.note: The vast Gothic 'pantheon of the doges', burial place of 25 of them, on a handsome campo beside Verrocchio's great equestrian Colleoni statue. Grand and richly furnished; often paired with the nearby Scuola Grande di San Marco façade.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Venice and its Lagoon

venues.name: Ponte dell'Accademia
venues.note: The wooden bridge by the Accademia gallery frames the single finest view of the Grand Canal sweeping down to the domes of the Salute, the picture every visitor wants. Best at sunset or in the soft light of early morning.

venues.name: Padua day trip
venues.note: Barely 15–25 minutes by fast train, Giotto's world-changing Scrovegni Chapel frescoes (timed booking essential), the huge Basilica of St Anthony, and Europe's oldest botanical garden. An easy, rewarding half- or full-day escape from the lagoon.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Padua's fourteenth-century fresco cycles

venues.name: Verona day trip
venues.note: About an hour by train, the Roman Arena (opera under the stars in summer), Juliet's balcony, and a graceful pink-marble old town on the Adige. Time a visit around the opera festival for an unforgettable evening; a private car makes the door-to-door version effortless.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, City of Verona

venues.name: Vicenza and the Palladian villas
venues.note: Palladio's own city, 45 minutes by train, the Teatro Olimpico, the Basilica Palladiana, and just outside town the perfect Villa La Rotonda that shaped Western architecture. Combine with a Brenta Riviera cruise past the aristocracy's summer villas on the way back.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, City of Vicenza and the Palladian Villas of the Veneto

venues.name: Bar Longhi, The Gritti Palace
venues.note: A jewel-box bar of gilt and Murano glass, opening to a Grand Canal terrace, the most elegant cocktail in Venice.
credentials: Inside The Gritti Palace (MICHELIN Two Keys, Luxury Collection), a landmark hotel bar

venues.name: Harry's Bar
venues.note: The 1931 birthplace of the Bellini, a wood-panelled ground-floor bar that is a piece of Venetian history in itself.
credentials: Declared a national landmark by Italy's Ministry of Culture (2001)

venues.name: Caffè Florian
venues.note: The oldest café in the world still trading, 1720, under the arcades of St Mark's, an orchestra playing on the square.
credentials: Founded 1720, the world's oldest continuously-operating café
Historic landmark of Piazza San Marco

venues.name: Bar Terrazza Danieli
venues.note: The Danieli's rooftop terrace over the lagoon, the Salute, San Giorgio and the basin spread out at sunset.
credentials: Atop Danieli, Venezia, A Four Seasons Hotel, a landmark rooftop

venues.name: Experimental Cocktail Club (Il Palazzo Experimental)
venues.area: Giudecca / Dorsoduro (Fondamenta Zattere allo Spirito Santo)
venues.note: The Paris-and-London group's Venetian outpost, the city's most serious contemporary cocktails, on the Zattere.
credentials: Part of the acclaimed Experimental Group, internationally recognised bar group

venues.name: Skyline Rooftop Bar, Hilton Molino Stucky
venues.note: An eighth-floor rooftop over the Giudecca canal, the widest panorama of the Venetian skyline over a drink.
credentials: A landmark rooftop bar, the highest public terrace on the Giudecca waterfront
